conflict_topics: naming companies / corporate accountability for fires
health impacts on children and ongoing illness after smoke clears
dialogue_quality_notes: Conversation is concise and personal: participants repeatedly anchor discussion in family/children and local impacts (e.g. 'my mother', 'my sister', 'my son').
Public environment updates structure the dialogue and introduce substantive new facts; participants react naturally to those updates.
Moderate repetition around schools, children and coughing, but not excessive.
No role confusion; speakers consistently reference their own local conditions and the updates.
evaluation.final_reason: By Round 15 a public update reported concrete official actions: a joint task force to trace corporate links, notices/investigations and revoked concessions, and rain had put out most fires (environment update). Agent B then said explicitly, "Thank God it's over. The schools are open again." (Turn 30). This matches Agent A's earlier demand to "Name the companies. That's the only way this will stop." (Turn 21) and addresses Agent B's priority of schools reopening. The combination of government action (investigations/notices/concession revocations) and the rain that ended active fires produced settlement of the participants' outstanding disagreement about accountability versus immediate reopening.
position_change_notes: Agent A initially pushed for naming companies as the solution (Turn 21). The public updates later reported investigations/notices and other actions; participants subsequently accepted that the crisis had ended (Round 15), so A's demand was effectively addressed by external actions.
Agent B's immediate priority was reopening schools (Turn 22). By Round 15 Agent B reported schools were open again (Turn 30), indicating that their practical concern was resolved.

Agent C consistently stayed focused on family health and economic necessity; no substantial change in position, though the participant welcomed rain and later reported lingering coughing in family (Turns 25, 31).
No participant abandoned a stated position without reason; where positions shifted it was because environment updates and government actions changed the factual situation.

round_scores.evidence: Agent A and Agent B both expressed worry about PSI and school closures (Turns 1-2). No incompatible claims or demands.
Agent C and Agent D described health and school impacts in Kalimantan and Brunei (Turns 3-4). No disagreement.
Environment update then Agents A and B reported personal health/work impacts (Turns 5-6). No incompatible positions.
Agents C and D emphasised health risk to children and staying indoors (Turns 7-8). No substantive disagreement.
Agent C asserted Malaysian and Singaporean companies were linked to fires and Agent D agreed it worsened the problem (Turns 9-10). No opposing claims among participants.
Agent C and D agreed blaming Indonesia is easy and unhelpful (Turns 11-12). No conflict.
Agents A and B reacted angrily to an Indonesian official's remark; both expressed upset but did not disagree with each other (Turns 13-14).
Agent C rejected that the official spoke for their family; Agent D agreed focus should be on children (Turns 15-16). No conflict.
Agent C reported haze reaching Jakarta and Agent D expressed sympathy (Turns 17-18). No disagreement.
Agent C explained the economic necessity of riding a motorbike; Agent D sympathised (Turns 19-20). No incompatible demands.

Agent A pushed accountability: "Finally. Name the companies. That's the only way this will stop." (Turn 21). Agent B responded with a different immediate priority: reopening schools (Turn 22), indicating a minor divergence in expectations about what will solve the problem.

Agent C reported a child needing hospital care and Agent D expressed concern (Turns 23-24). The earlier minor disagreement (naming companies vs immediate school reopening) was not addressed and remained unresolved at the end of the round.

Environment update reported rain and improving air; Agents C and D reacted (Turns 25-26). The earlier minor disagreement about naming companies vs immediate relief was not settled in speech by participants and so persisted.
Agent C waited for news from their sister and Agent A noted improved air (Turns 27, 29). No resolution of the prior minor disagreement occurred.

A public update described official actions ("agreed to set up a joint task force to trace the money and corporate links...", rain put out most fires, and investigations/concessions revoked). Agent B responded: "Thank God it's over. The schools are open again." (Turn 30). Official actions plus participants' acceptance show the earlier small dispute over naming companies vs immediate reopening was addressed.
Agents exchanged condolences and hopes for recovery of sick children (Turns 32-33). No substantive conflict remained.

substantive_insights: Tension between seeking accountability (naming/holding companies to account) and the immediate practical need to reopen schools and restore daily life.
Economic necessity forces exposure: Agent C's claim ('If I don't ride, my family doesn't eat') highlights trade-off between health and livelihood.
Health impacts persist after visible smoke clears (participants note children still coughing after fires went out).
Resolution combined natural factors (rain) and official actions (investigations, concessions revoked), showing multiple causal paths to reducing haze.
